content.text:
Reviewed [PR #238 at `9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a`](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/commit/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a) against its verified `main` merge base, [`969512b37fc68935323e425ef40c9a9b62612f11`](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/commit/969512b37fc68935323e425ef40c9a9b62612f11).

- **P2 · A failed refresh can let a helper check in the wrong attendee.** The scanner keeps fresh confirmation enabled against cached ticket details after a refetch error. A completed transfer changes the owner in place and can leave both expected check-in counts unchanged. The helper can therefore see the former owner’s name and check in the recipient. Keep the outcome and same-key retry available after a failed refresh, require a successful lookup before a fresh confirmation, and compare the displayed owner with the locked row, as #219 does for manual check-in. EVO-128 already tracks the UI for transfers that are still open. [Scanner template](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/app/scanning/handle-registration/handle-registration.component.html#L40-L65) · [Confirm button](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/app/scanning/handle-registration/handle-registration.component.html#L381-L401) · [Transfer finalization](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/server/registrations/registration-transfer-finalization.ts#L1034-L1055) · [#219 owner check](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/219#discussion_r4658745564) · [EVO-128](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-128)
- **P2 · An open scanner tab breaks at deployment.** #238 documents that the new required fields reject older clients. A helper who loaded the scanner before rollout can lose the ability to confirm mid-event, and #219’s `checkInMethod` default covers only that field. Provide an explicit refresh path for old tabs and verify it across the deployment boundary. Preserve the requirement for an operation key and expected state on retryable writes. [#238 RPC contract](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/shared/rpc-contracts/app-rpcs/events.rpcs.ts#L204-L232) · [#219 compatibility review](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/219#discussion_r4658745667)

**Checks.** Static review confirmed that a matching key returns the recorded outcome before the cutoff check, and a fresh intent must pass the cutoff and locked-count checks. I inspected the PostgreSQL and Playwright coverage for duplicate guests and a lost response after commit. I also checked #219 at `e6dd3a1e`. The PRs document the integration work for whichever lands second, and the manual retry finding remains open there. I ran no runtime suites or combined build. GitHub check status could not be independently verified. [Replay handler](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/server/effect/rpc/handlers/events/events-registration.handlers.ts#L2604-L2649) · [Cutoff test](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/db/schema/registration-concurrency.postgres.spec.ts#L1629) · [Lost-response test](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/tests/specs/scanning/scanner.test.ts#L1280) · [#219 retry finding](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/219#discussion_r4658745565)

**Open for Lukas.** Should pending check-ins survive a reload, and how should the scanner present a queued request that first reaches the server after the two-hour post-event cutoff? This remains a product decision outside #238. [EVO-26 plan, November 18](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-26#comment-33ac0bf6-58ad-41a4-a3ad-a260e358fd65)

[PR #238](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/238) makes door check-in more reliable on weak connections. It loads the ticket and add-ons together, shows whether check-in was confirmed, and safely retries the same request if the response drops. That matches [EVO-26](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-26). I reviewed head `9b2c70dd` against `main` merge base `969512b3`.

- **P2 · Verified from the contract: pre-deployment scanner tabs lose the ability to confirm.** Helpers with an open tab will need to reload mid-event because the new server requires fields their client cannot send. Those fields support safe retries, and an explicit refresh path would address the rollout disruption. [RPC contract](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/shared/rpc-contracts/app-rpcs/events.rpcs.ts#L204-L232)
- **P2 · Possible in use: a failed refresh can lead to checking in the wrong attendee.** The template allows a fresh confirmation using cached details after a refresh fails. If the ticket changed owners, the helper can still see the former owner’s name while admitting the recipient. Keeping the outcome and same-request retry visible is necessary for recovery. Fresh confirmation should require a successful lookup and an owner check under the lock. EVO-128 already covers the distinct case of an open transfer. [Scanner template](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/app/scanning/handle-registration/handle-registration.component.html#L381-L401) · [Transfer ownership update](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/server/registrations/registration-transfer-finalization.ts#L1034-L1055) · [EVO-128](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-128)

Static review confirmed that a recorded request can replay after cutoff and a fresh request must pass the cutoff and count checks. The operation record and combined lookup support the stated scope. I found no other broader changes that need action in #238. The manual check-in integration remains tracked on [#219](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/219#discussion_r4658745565). I did not run runtime suites or a combined build, and GitHub check status remained unverified.

**Open for Lukas.** Should pending check-ins survive a reload, and what should helpers see if a queued request first reaches the server after the two-hour post-event cutoff? [EVO-26 product question](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-26#comment-33ac0bf6-58ad-41a4-a3ad-a260e358fd65)

During the prototype phase, we do not care about any incompatiblity issues, much less about such a narrow one.
Please explain the second issue to me

I’d drop the compatibility finding for the prototype. The second finding is about **the name the helper sees versus the owner the server checks in**.

1. A helper scans Alice’s ticket and leaves the preview open.
2. Alice’s ticket is transferred to Bob. The transfer changes the owner but keeps the same registration ID. Both the attendee and guest check-in counts can stay at zero.
3. The scanner tries to refresh the preview, but the connection drops. PR #238 keeps showing the cached preview, so the helper still sees Alice and can press **Confirm check-in**.
4. The connection recovers and the confirmation reaches the server. The registration now belongs to Bob. The counts still match, and the request carries no expected owner, so the server can mark Bob as checked in.

I verified that the code permits this sequence. I didn’t reproduce it in a browser. It’s a narrow race that requires a completed transfer while the preview is open and a failed refresh. The fix is to keep **Try again** available for an already-sent request, but bind any fresh confirmation to the attendee shown on screen. [Scanner template](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/app/scanning/handle-registration/handle-registration.component.html#L381-L401) · [Transfer ownership update](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/server/registrations/registration-transfer-finalization.ts#L1034-L1055)
Why would it keep the same registration ID?

Evorto treats a transfer as **changing who owns an existing ticket**. It updates the owner on the same registration row and creates a new acquisition record for the recipient. The registration ID identifies the ticket entry, while the acquisition records how its owner got it. [Transfer finalization](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/server/registrations/registration-transfer-finalization.ts#L1034-L1070)

The practical reason to keep the ID is that the same entry still represents a place in the same event. That’s my reading of the design. For the scanner, the consequence is that looking up the same ID can now return a different person. A confirmation should also carry the attendee the helper saw.
That seems very complicated, previously we just cancelled the original registration and created a new one for the new owner, give me the pros and cons on this
I’ll compare what each model means for ticket validity, event capacity, payments, and the scanner.

content.text:
**Keeping the registration ID makes it simpler to carry the same reserved place through a transfer. Cancelling and creating a new registration makes it simpler to tell whose ticket you’re looking at.** Both models can preserve capacity, and both still need to handle payments and refunds.

| | Keep the registration ID | Cancel the original and create a new registration |
|---|---|---|
| **Capacity and add-ons** | The same registration continues to hold the place. References can stay attached, which helps when the event or an add-on is sold out. | The transfer must hand the reservation to the new registration atomically. Ordinary cancellation followed by ordinary booking could release the place to someone else, trigger a waitlist update, or fail on a sold-out add-on. |
| **QR codes and check-in** | A QR with the registration ID can now resolve to a different attendee. A scanner confirmation needs to carry the owner the helper saw. | The old QR points to a cancelled ticket, and the recipient gets a new QR. A stale preview of the original can be rejected by checking its status. |
| **History and personal data** | Anything that needs to know who owned or paid for the ticket at a specific time needs ownership history. The transfer also has to explicitly replace owner-specific data. Evorto already replaces the original registration answers with the recipient’s. | Each owner has their own registration row, which makes answers and attendance history easier to interpret. The rows still need a transfer link so reporting can distinguish a handoff from an unrelated cancellation and new sale. |
| **Payments and refunds** | Payments and refunds must be tied to the right ownership period. Evorto records a new acquisition for the buyer and ties the seller’s refund to the seller’s original transaction. | Separate rows make that ownership easier to see. You still need to coordinate the buyer’s payment, the seller’s refund, and retries if any step fails. |

[Evorto’s transfer finalization](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/blob/9b2c70dd7d7287f847611f2efa1c421bcc01cc9a/src/server/registrations/registration-transfer-finalization.ts#L1034-L1142)

If the product rule is **“the seller’s ticket becomes invalid and the buyer gets their own ticket,”** the old model expresses that directly and avoids the scanner race we discussed. Its main cost is implementing the handoff as one transfer operation so the reserved place and any transferable add-ons move together.
